chapter: Sidney Bechet and the Paris festival
title: The Rendezvous in Philadelphia and Lee Guber's offer
summary: The club owner suggested Moore lead his own group, which annoyed Bechet.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: We were contracted to play on Walnut Street in Philadelphia, the Rendezvous, so we were there a few days --
In West Philadelphia was that? The Rendezvous?

In the center of Philadelphia, Walnut Street in the Hotel Senator, it's not there any more and I got such a great reception there with my playing and my solo work that after the job one night the man that owned the place came to me and said, 'These people go for you, Chief. Why don't you come back with your own group at a later time?' So he gave me the idea --
Okay, you were talking about another Bechet --
Yes, the owner of the place was Lee Guber who married Barbara Walters in later years, divorced her -- Lee came to me and said, 'These people

go for you, Chief. I got an idea. I think you'd do good in this house. Why don't you make your own group and come back at some time, when I need an attraction." I said, "I'll keep this in mind, Mr. Guber." And it got to Sidney and Sidney didn't like it, naturally. But I finished the job with him and never came back until a sufficient time elapsed before I'd come back with my own group. That's one of the stories that I'd like to tell you that I was beginning to like the idea of being a band leader.
You had never before that time led a band, led a small group, you were always with other musicians.

I was always -- at the Central Plaza and the Stuyvesant Casino I've already said who I worked with, many of those people were great, great and I have that Stuyvesant Nights album (Stycon 100) to tape.
